Every value in the tables below was read out of the render that produced this page.
The filter is enabled in this site's `_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
filters:
  - lua-env
```

## Pandoc

| Source | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `{{{< lua-env pandoc.FORMAT >}}}` | {{< lua-env pandoc.FORMAT >}} |
| `{{{< lua-env pandoc.PANDOC_VERSION >}}}` | {{< lua-env pandoc.PANDOC_VERSION >}} |
| `{{{< lua-env pandoc.PANDOC_API_VERSION >}}}` | {{< lua-env pandoc.PANDOC_API_VERSION >}} |

: Pandoc globals, as this page was written. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[55,45]"}

Render the same document to another format and `pandoc.FORMAT` changes with it.

## Deeper paths

The argument is one dot-separated path, and it reaches as far down the tree as you need.
A key that holds a hyphen needs no quoting, because the path is split on the full stop alone.

| Source | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `{{{< lua-env pandoc.PANDOC_WRITER_OPTIONS.wrap_text >}}}` | {{< lua-env pandoc.PANDOC_WRITER_OPTIONS.wrap_text >}} |
| `{{{< lua-env pandoc.PANDOC_WRITER_OPTIONS.html_math_method.method >}}}` | {{< lua-env pandoc.PANDOC_WRITER_OPTIONS.html_math_method.method >}} |
| `{{{< lua-env quarto.doc.language.back-to-top >}}}` | {{< lua-env quarto.doc.language.back-to-top >}} |
| `{{{< lua-env quarto.project.offset >}}}` | {{< lua-env quarto.project.offset >}} |

: Deeper paths, as this page was rendered. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[70,30]"}

The first two rows are options Quarto hands to Pandoc for this format.
The third is one of Quarto's own interface strings, in the language the document declares.
The fourth is the path from this page back to the root of the project, so a page in a subdirectory prints something else.

::: {.callout-note}
Some of what the extension reports describes the machine that ran the render.
`quarto.version`, `pandoc.PANDOC_VERSION` and `pandoc.PANDOC_API_VERSION` are the versions installed there, so a local preview and the published build print different numbers.
`pandoc.FORMAT` and the interface strings follow the document instead, and stay the same wherever it is rendered.
:::

::: {.callout-important}
`quarto.version` is the only list the shortcode joins, and it joins it with full stops.
Every other list prints its items one after another with nothing between them, so `{{{< lua-env pandoc.PANDOC_WRITER_OPTIONS.extensions >}}}` gives {{< lua-env pandoc.PANDOC_WRITER_OPTIONS.extensions >}} here.
:::

## Through the `meta` shortcode

Everything sits under the `lua-env` metadata key as well, so Quarto's own shortcode reaches it without the extension's own:

| Source | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `{{{< meta lua-env.pandoc.FORMAT >}}}` | {{< meta lua-env.pandoc.FORMAT >}} |

: The same value, read as ordinary metadata. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[55,45]"}

::: {.callout-note}
The two shortcodes are not interchangeable.
`meta` prints scalars, and reports `?invalid meta type` for anything else, so a path such as `lua-env.quarto.version`, which is a list of three numbers, needs the extension's own shortcode.
:::

## When a path does not resolve

None of the calls in this section run on this page, because each one writes a message the build would report.

A call with no argument gives two messages and renders nothing:

```markdown
{{{< lua-env >}}}
```

```text
(E) [lua-env] The "lua-env" shortcode needs its "variable" argument.
(W) [lua-env] No variable name provided.
```

A path whose last part is absent gives one warning and renders nothing:

```markdown
{{{< lua-env pandoc.NOPE >}}}
```

```text
(W) [lua-env] Variable 'pandoc.NOPE' not found in lua-env metadata.
```

Two other shapes stop the render instead of reporting it:

- A path whose middle part is absent, such as `pandoc.NOPE.name`, fails with `attempt to index a nil value`.
- A path that names a branch rather than a value, such as `pandoc.PANDOC_WRITER_OPTIONS`, fails with `Inline expected, got table`.

Read a path off the tree in [What is published](reference.qmd#what-is-published) before you use it.

## Exporting to JSON

This site leaves the export off, since it would write host paths into a file the site then publishes:

```yaml
extensions:
  lua-env:
    json: false
```

Turning it on writes `lua-env.json` beside the source document, so add it to `.gitignore`:

```yaml
extensions:
  lua-env:
    json: true
```

Narrow it to what you actually want, and the file stays readable:

```yaml
extensions:
  lua-env:
    json: true
    json-include:
      - pandoc.FORMAT
      - quarto.version
```

Or keep everything except one noisy branch:

```yaml
extensions:
  lua-env:
    json: true
    json-exclude:
      - quarto._quarto
```

You can use both at once.
The exclusion wins, so it drops a branch from inside what the inclusion kept:

```yaml
extensions:
  lua-env:
    json: true
    json-include: pandoc.PANDOC_WRITER_OPTIONS
    json-exclude: pandoc.PANDOC_WRITER_OPTIONS.extensions
```

Either option also takes a single path, as above, rather than a list.

::: {.callout-warning}
`json-exclude-sensitive` defaults to `true` and drops the input file, the output file, the project directories, and the Pandoc script path.
Leave it on unless the file stays on your own machine.
:::

### Naming the export file

`json-file` names the file, and the extension reads it only when `json` is `true`:

```yaml
extensions:
  lua-env:
    json: true
    json-file: "_build/lua-env.json"
```

The path is resolved against the directory of the source document.
A document in `posts/first/` therefore writes `posts/first/_build/lua-env.json`, whatever the project root and the output directory are.

The extension writes the file but does not create the directory above it.
A directory that is absent is reported, and the render carries on without an export:

```text
(E) [lua-env] Failed to write JSON file: _build/lua-env.json: No such file or directory
```

An empty `json-file` falls back to `lua-env.json`.

### What the redaction leaves behind

A redacted path is removed with everything under it.
`quarto.project` is not itself a redacted path, but two of its three entries are:

```yaml
extensions:
  lua-env:
    json: true
    json-include: quarto.project
```

For a document at the root of its project, that writes:

```json
{
  "quarto": {
    "project": {
      "offset": "."
    }
  }
}
```

Set the option to `false` to keep the two that were dropped:

```yaml
extensions:
  lua-env:
    json: true
    json-exclude-sensitive: false
```

[Redacted paths](reference.qmd#redacted-paths) lists everything the option removes.

### Exporting from a build server

`json-warn-on-server` is `true` unless you set it.
With the export on, and one of the continuous integration variables set, the filter warns once and still writes the file:

```text
(W) [lua-env] JSON export is enabled in a server/CI context (CI is set). The exported file may leak host filesystem paths. Set extensions.lua-env.json-warn-on-server: false to silence this warning.
```

Silence the warning once you have decided the export is safe there:

```yaml
extensions:
  lua-env:
    json: true
    json-warn-on-server: false
```

A variable that is empty, or set to the text `false`, does not count as a build server.
The check belongs to the export alone.
With `json: false` the extension writes no file and reports no warning, whatever the environment holds.
[JSON export](reference.qmd#json-export) names the variables the check looks at.
